Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Onramp lanes & term credit allocation — Voyant capacity plan

Hi Aiden,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As promised, attaching a draft commit matrix that lays out a lane-based onramp for Dedicated capacity (GPU + TPM) across a 3-year term. The goal here is to give Voyant the flexibility to concentrate spend in Year 1 (if you want a steeper discount) or smooth the commits across the term for lower near-term cash.

Key points in the spreadsheet:
- Lane A / Year 1 frontload option: 40% Year 1, 30% Year 2, 30% Year 3 (largest discount band)
- Lane B / Smooth ramp: 25% / 35% / 40% (moderate discount)
- Invoice cadence choices: annual prepay, annual invoice with prepay credit, or quarterly invoicing against prepaid credit
- Optional escrow for Year 1 prepay to satisfy procurement oversight (we can populate an escrow clause).

Attachments: voyant_onramp_commit_matrix.xlsx, redwood_term_sheet_v2.pdf (term sheet with discount tiers).

Highlights I want to call out: if you elect Lane A and prepay Year 1 we can move to a 12-18% effective term discount vs list, combined with a 6-8% amortized credit applied over Year 1 invoices (helps cash modeling on your side). If you prefer smoothing, the discount is shallower but we can add a small usage buffer for burst months.

Would you and Lina be available next week to go through the matrix line-by-line? If you share your preferred invoice cadence and whether procurement will require escrow/sign-off, I can draft a counterproposal that matches Voyant's cash profile.

Best,
Grace
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Onramp lanes & term credit allocation — Voyant capacity plan

Grace — thanks for the clear matrix and the call recap. A few quick items from our side after a rapid pass with Lina:

1) Procurement will push for as much of Year 1 to be classified as a prepay (they're asking for payment terms that favor credit recognition on our P&L now).
2) That said, cash is tighter than expected in Q1 of FY27; a 100% frontload isn't realistic. We want to see if we can structure a 50% Year 1 prepay (higher than your Lane B, lower than Lane A) and still get close to the Lane A economics.
3) Can Redwood provide a simple amortization schedule (12 vs 36 months) showing how a 50% prepay maps to the effective per-token/unit price? Lina also wants to know what the break points are for deeper discounts (what threshold moves us from 12% to 15% effective term discount).
4) Also: procurement is likely to ask for a short escrow instrument or a bank guarantee for the Year 1 funds — is that something Redwood supports or can we partner with EscrowCo?

If you can send a redlined term sheet that shows a 50% Year 1 prepay and the resulting discount bands, we'll share it with legal/procurement.

Thanks,
Aiden
VP Engineering — Voyant.ai
+1 646-555-2341
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 08:10:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Onramp lanes & term credit allocation — quick pricing tilt suggestion

Grace / Marissa — forwarding Aiden's note. Quick thoughts:
- We can accept a 50% Year 1 prepay but should condition the deepest discount bucket on a modest commitment to Year 2 (>= 25%). That avoids them taking early consumption and dropping out.
- Offer: 50% Year 1 prepay + Year 2 minimum of 25% (by commit, not cash) -> unlocks a 14% effective term discount; 60% Year 1 frontload unlocks 16%.
- Escrow: we can accommodate third-party escrow; legal will need language about release triggers tied to consumption milestones. That keeps our revenue recognition clean and gives Voyant procurement comfort.

I'll help price the amortization models. Grace, can you run a 12mo vs 36mo amortization table for the 50% and 60% prepay scenarios and drop into the spreadsheet? Marissa, looping you for any operational constraints on burst buffers when they frontload.

—Ben
VP Sales — Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Aiden Brooks <aiden@voyant.ai>, Lina Torres <procurement@voyant.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 26 May 2026 10:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onramp lanes & term credit allocation — Voyant capacity plan

Aiden / Lina — appreciate the transparency on cash cadence. Attached I put a short counterproposal and two amortization tables (12m vs 36m) for the 50% prepay and an alternate 60% frontload. Key elements:

- Commercial ask: 50% Year 1 prepay + minimum Year 2 commit of 25% by volume (not necessarily prepaid) -> effective term discount 14% (12mo amortization) or 13% (36mo).
- Frontload sweetener: 60% Year 1 prepay moves to 16% effective term discount and gives an additional 5% buffer for burst months in Year 1.
- Escrow: Redwood will accept escrow or a bank guarantee. We'll add escrow release milestones: (a) 25% release on contract execution, (b) remaining released pro rata as invoiced consumption hits monthly thresholds, final release at 12 months or on early termination per standard terms.
- Invoicing: we can do annual prepay + quarterly consumption reports. If you prefer monthly invoicing against credit, we'll add a small admin fee (0.5%) to cover the cadence.
- Implementation: Monica (CS) will own onboarding milestones; we'll include a 4-week onboarding credit to help with initial training runs.

Attachments: voyant_onramp_commit_matrix.xlsx (updated, tab: counterproposal), redwood_term_sheet_v2.pdf (redline).

If that structure looks OK, I'll produce a redlined term sheet for your legal and a DocuSign envelope for signatures. Proposed next step: Lina / Procurement to confirm escrow preference and Voyager's internal approval window.

Best,
Grace

1) Can you convert the amortization table into an effective $/token equivalent for both 50%/60% prepay so our product finance can plug it into their unit economics model?
2) For the escrow instrument: procurement prefers a third-party escrow (EscrowCo). Can Redwood accept EscrowCo with release triggers as you outlined? If so, please share the escrow agreement template so our legal can review in parallel.

If we get those two items today or Monday, I'll route to legal and we should be able to sign next week. We prefer DocuSign for the execution.

Thanks — looking forward to locking this in.
Aiden
